S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.

subtypes.Racing Thoughts: Thoughts spinning too fast in the head, constantly jumping from one idea to another.
subtypes.Flooding of Thoughts: Too many thoughts emerging simultaneously, making them disorganized.
subtypes.Inability to Control Thoughts: Unable to stop or slow down thoughts and unable to calm the mind.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

info.persona: Dominique Puma balances a competitive quilting spirit with a love for heritage gardening, meticulously plans every project while they sometimes hoard coupons and forget to relax.
info.professional_persona: Dominique Puma, a retired community project coordinator turned budding historical society leader and home‑based boutique entrepreneur, leverages meticulous organization, budgeting expertise, and a skeptical, competitive eye to streamline event planning, preserve local heritage, and win craft contests, and they consistently apply these strengths to every community initiative.
info.cultural_background: Dominique grew up in Pineville, Avoyelles Parish, a region where Southern hospitality blends with French‑Acadian heritage. As a white Southern woman, she was raised in a Protestant household that emphasized church involvement, family gatherings, and respect for local traditions such as Mardi Gras and Cajun folklore. Her upbringing instilled a strong work ethic, a pragmatic approach to life, and a deep appreciation for the culinary and musical traditions of Louisiana, while her curiosity encourages her to explore broader cultural influences.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Dominique spends her free time cultivating a vibrant garden of native herbs, peppers, and okra, which fuels her love for cooking traditional Creole dishes. She enjoys quilting and crochet, often entering local contests where her competitive nature shines. Her curiosity drives her deep dive into genealogy, chronicling her family’s lineage in a personal archive. She relaxes with historical fiction set in the American South, participates in church potluck gatherings, and occasionally bird‑watches in the nearby Atchafalaya wetlands.
info.sports_persona: Dominique Puma, an enthusiastic supporter of the LSU Tigers football and the New Orleans Saints, keeps fit through daily garden labor, weekly tai chi classes at the senior center, occasional paddle‑boarding on the Atchafalaya during summer, and they cheer loudly at local high‑school softball games.
info.arts_persona: Dominique Puma, a dedicated participant in the regional quilting circuit, draws inspiration from folk artist Clementine Hunter and the accordion melodies of BeauSoleil, often listening to Bobby Charles while stitching, and they find solace in the historical novels of Marjorie Kinnan Rawlings.
info.travel_persona: Dominique Puma, a methodical planner who favors well‑researched itineraries and modest budgets, has explored the historic streets of New Orleans and the bayous of Louisiana, and they now dream of tracing French‑Acadian roots with a cultural immersion trip to Normandy, France, and a culinary pilgrimage to Martinique.
info.culinary_persona: Dominique Puma, a skilled Creole home chef, regularly prepares gumbo with homegrown okra, smoked andouille, and a blend of thyme and cayenne, delights in preserving pickled peppers and making roux for étouffée, and they indulge in occasional fine‑dining outings for fresh oysters and crawfish étouffée at The Chimes.

info.persona: Richard Michaelian is a curiously disorganized retiree who blends strategic business insight, art‑centered community work, garden‑fresh cooking, and a love of photography while mentoring startups and chasing European art pilgrimages.
info.professional_persona: Richard Michaelian, a retired corporate strategist with 35 years of business leadership, now channels their negotiating prowess and community‑organizing energy into mentoring local start‑ups, curating exhibitions for the Wareham Arts Council, and drafting a memoir that fuses business lessons with artistic reflections, all while embracing a relaxed, flexible approach to scheduling.
info.cultural_background: Richard grew up in post‑war New England, shaped by a blend of traditional New England values and his family's Armenian heritage. Raised in Plymouth County, he was immersed in the region’s maritime culture, community gatherings, and a strong emphasis on education. Family traditions brought Armenian holidays, cuisine, and storytelling into his upbringing, fostering a respect for cultural diversity and a love for sharing heritage through food and community events.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Richard enjoys a vibrant social calendar that includes weekly visits to the local art museum, attending community theater productions, and participating in a seniors' book club focused on history and philosophy. He cultivates a vegetable garden, practices landscape photography of the New England coastline, plays bridge at the town’s senior center, and takes part in weekend fishing trips on Buzzards Bay. His curiosity also leads him to experiment with cooking dishes from various cultures, especially Armenian recipes handed down by his grandparents.
info.sports_persona: Richard Michaelian enjoys low‑impact fitness like sunrise walks along Buzzards Bay, occasional kayaking with the Cape Cod Sailing Club, avidly follows the Boston Red Sox and New England Patriots, and plays bridge at the senior center as their mental sport while joining the Wareham Gatemen fan club for weekend baseball outings.
info.arts_persona: Richard Michaelian spends their weeks wandering the local art museum, giving informal tours that weave in Monet’s Impressionism and Ansel Adams’s coastal photography, participates in community theater productions of classic plays, and practices watercolor painting inspired by Georgia O’Keeffe while curating showcases that highlight emerging regional artists.
info.travel_persona: Richard Michaelian dreams of strolling the Uffizi in Florence and savoring Viennese coffee house culture, but their travel planning remains loosely organized; they often book last‑minute trips using senior discounts, favor destinations where they can photograph rugged coastlines—like Maine’s Acadia National Park—or combine art museum visits with family reunions in Martha’s Vineyard.
info.culinary_persona: Richard Michaelian delights in preparing Armenian dolma and khorovats using herbs from their vegetable garden, pairs them with fresh New England clams, and experiments with Mediterranean tagines, though their occasional forgetfulness leads to over‑simmering sauces, prompting them to keep a handwritten recipe notebook beside their kitchen sink.

info.persona: Myra Lee is a fiercely imaginative 20‑year‑old pipefitting apprentice who balances eco‑focused technical work with a passion for art, community mentorship, and a tendency to over‑think when anxiety strikes.
info.professional_persona: Myra Lee is a 20‑year‑old pipefitting apprentice in Miami, combining precise blueprint interpretation, welding, and hydraulic maintenance with a flair for integrating artistic design into sustainable water‑system projects, and they channel their imaginative curiosity and collaborative nature into mentoring peers while constantly seeking innovative, eco‑friendly installation methods.
info.cultural_background: Myra is an African‑American woman raised in the multicultural tapestry of Miami Beach. Her family blends Southern Black traditions with Caribbean influences from relatives who emigrated from Jamaica, resulting in a rich cultural mix of music, food, and community values. She grew up attending a historically Black church that emphasized collective responsibility and social justice, which fuels her compassionate drive to help others. The vibrant Afro‑Latino neighborhoods, the sounds of reggae, hip‑hop, and salsa, and the visual language of street murals have shaped her artistic sensibility and reinforced her commitment to uplifting her community through both her trade and her creative pursuits.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Myra nurtures her artistic side through painting, sketching, and digital illustration, often drawing inspiration from Miami’s vibrant street art and coastal scenery. She enjoys exploring contemporary art galleries, reading science‑fiction and speculative design books, and photographing urban architecture. To manage her intense emotional reactivity, she practices yoga, meditation, and occasional journaling. She also volunteers at a local community center, where she mentors high‑school students interested in skilled trades and participates in neighborhood clean‑up and water‑conservation initiatives.
info.sports_persona: Myra Lee enjoys the rhythmic energy of beach volleyball at a local club and follows the Miami Heat and Inter Miami CF avidly, playing pickup basketball on weekends while they occasionally join a community running group that meets for early‑morning jogs along the shoreline.
info.arts_persona: Myra Lee nurtures a vibrant artistic life, frequenting the Pérez Art Museum to study works by Kehinde Wiley and Banksy, sketching urban murals inspired by Caribbean reggae rhythms and hip‑hop beats from artists like Bob Marley and Missy Elliott, and creating digital illustrations that blend sci‑fi motifs with Miami’s coastal colors.
info.travel_persona: Myra Lee prefers purposeful travel that blends relaxation with cultural immersion, having explored the beaches of Jamaica and the historic streets of New Orleans, while they dream of studying sustainable architecture in Iceland and plan a budget‑friendly road trip along the Florida Keys to document coastal ecosystems.
info.culinary_persona: Myra Lee’s palate mixes Caribbean spice with coastal freshness, favoring jerk chicken, conch fritters, and mango‑coconut salsa, and while they are a modest home cook, they enjoy experimenting with plant‑based fish tacos using fresh local catch, often pairing meals with a chilled glass of hibiscus tea.
